t.E1452.agn: In 2008 EFSA set the tolerable weekly intake (TWI) at 1 mg/kg body weight and reported that this limit may be exceeded in a significant part of the European population. The main sources are cereals, vegetables and drinks; the contribution of additives could not be quantified.
t.E1452.body: Aluminium is very poorly absorbed from food (about 0.1%), but the absorbed part may accumulate in tissues, especially bone.
t.E1452.eff.0.t: Aluminium intake from all sources may exceed the weekly limit; the absorbed part may accumulate in tissues. The contribution of additives could not be quantified
t.E1452.eff.0.w: A significant part of the European population
t.E1452.prod: Produced by esterifying starch with octenyl succinic anhydride and treating it with aluminium sulphate (modified starch).
t.E1452.regx.0: Weekly limit for the whole diet 1 mg/kg; may be exceeded in part of the population.
t.E1452.summary: A modified starch containing aluminium. It is used as a coating in vitamin supplements.
t.E1452.what: A modified starch used as a capsule material and carrier in supplement and vitamin preparations.
